Earlier reports from Counterpoint Research have already shown that Apple posted its strongest-ever second-quarter iPhone shipment performance, and now Omdia has released its own data, which points to the same record-breaking result. Here's the full breakdown.

Omdia warns that the steepest declines are still ahead

Earlier, we reported on a Counterpoint Research report that released preliminary data on global smartphone shipments for Q2 2026.

Counterpoint noted in its report that Samsung led the market with a 24% shipment share, up from 20% a year earlier; Apple followed closely at 20%, also up from 17% last year. Xiaomi dropped from 14% to 12%, OPPO fell from 12% to 11%, and vivo slipped from 9% to 8%.

Now, Omdia's preliminary report (via MacMagazine) points to the same overall trend, though its estimated figures differ slightly.

Omdia places Samsung's shipment share at 22%, up from 20% in Q2 2025; Apple follows closely at 20%, up from 16% last year. Xiaomi dropped from 15% to 11%, OPPO fell from 12% to 10%, and vivo slipped from 9% to 8%.

Below is Omdia's commentary on Apple's performance this quarter:

As expected, Omdia noted that the ongoing memory chip crunch caused overall shipments to fall 4% year-over-year, making Q2 2026 the weakest quarter for the market since Q2 2023.
